cpu: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core (128 threads), AVX-512, 1 TB RAM
method: emulation (plan-blessed): CPU prefill measured via a PyTorch forward pass; GPU decode ITL from the aggregated GPU run
caveat: CPU forward time was dominated by a large, variable fixed overhead (~128-166 s/forward) consistent with reading the ~16 GB model off the network filesystem each call; RAM-staging (.clone(), /dev/shm) did not fully resolve it. Absolute times are therefore I/O-bound, not compute-bound. The optimized vLLM CPU backend (source build) would be needed for a precise ceiling.
headline: CPU prefill (~100-600 tok/s) is ~20-110x slower than GPU prefill (~10,780 tok/s) for the same 8B model -> Config E sacrifices TTFT by 1-2 orders of magnitude, confirming H2's premise. The viable regime (short ISL, decode-bound OSL, throughput-oriented SLO, idle CPU) is narrow.
